blindSummary: This country is the region's leader on trans legal protection. Same-sex relations were decriminalised in 2010; the 2013 constitution bans discrimination on the basis of gender identity AND expression — reportedly the only constitution in the world with that explicit pairing. Counterweights: no gender-marker change mechanism, and a regional trans-rights network documents high rates of violence and harassment against trans people. The capital has an organised community, including a local house community and an LGBTQ+ pride organisation.
blindOutOfScope: Constitutional protection versus a documented street-violence gap.
blindSourceSummaries: International LGBT-rights organisation country overview (updated March 2026): same-sex relations decriminalised 2010; this country's constitution bans discrimination based on sexual orientation and gender identity/expression (2013 constitution, first enshrined 1997 - among the first countries worldwide); workplace protections since 2007; health professionals prohibited from attempting to change sexual orientation; an indigenous traditional third-gender role exists, but there is no legal gender recognition procedure.

A regional human-rights alliance's policy brief and case study on legal gender recognition in this country (2023): despite the world-leading constitutional protection, legislative and policy frameworks do not permit gender-marker changes or recognise third-gender identities; trans people face high rates of violence, abuse and harassment and are marginalised in public, private and political sectors.

LGBTQ+ news outlet (July 2006): the country's overseas mission confirmed men engaging in consensual gay sex would no longer be arrested - welcomed by a foreign HIV charity as a step for the human rights of 'gay citizens and tourists' and for HIV prevention; notes the country's constitutional protections.

Travel-news archive country report: the 1997 constitution was the second in the world to protect against sexual-orientation discrimination; a 2006 policy stopped arresting men for consensual gay sex; legal since Feb 2010 under reformed crimes legislation; no same-sex marriage recognition (barred since 2002); the president launched a 2011 UN report on men who have sex with men, trans people and HIV.

Foreign broadsheet (April 2005): the prime minister rejected international pressure to legalise gay sex, calling homosexuality a sin - after an overseas tourist and a local man received two-year jail sentences for sex; they were freed on bail pending an appeal arguing the constitution's non-discrimination clause overrides the penal code.
blindLocalsOnly: No gender-marker change mechanism — resident-facing; the violence and harassment rates documented by a regional trans-rights network describe residents' experience.
blindTangential: The 2010 decriminalisation removed same-sex-conduct exposure for visitors travelling with partners.
